labels.text: List the account's artifacts, newest first.

S26.02.needs: a signed-in account with artifacts (Managed mode, not Local); one artifact with no title for the fallback check
S26.02.note: The CLI has no card or viewer, so the title appears only on the list row and in --json output.
steps: Open a terminal and run: agi artifacts list
Find a row: the title sits between the artifact id and the [type] tag
Check that an artifact with no title shows Untitled artifact
Compare with Expected: the title shows on the row (no card or viewer exists in the CLI); agi artifacts show <id> --json also carries the title

labels.text: List the account's artifacts, newest first.

S26.03.needs: a signed-in account with artifacts of more than one kind (Managed mode)
S26.03.note: The type is shown only as the raw stored value in brackets, with no card or viewer and no human-readable kind name.
steps: Run: agi artifacts list
Look at the [bracketed] tag after each title
Compare the tag with the kind named in Expected (for example html, react, svg, mermaid, markdown, text, code)

labels.text: Print an artifact's content, or write it to a file.
List the account's artifacts, newest first.

S26.05.needs: a signed-in account with at least one artifact (Managed mode)
S26.05.note: The view is terminal output; the in-chat form /artifacts show <id> exists only in Managed mode and no in-chat artifact link was found.
steps: Run: agi artifacts list and copy one id from the first column
Run: agi artifacts show <that id>
Look: the artifact's content prints in the terminal
Optionally run agi artifacts open <id> to open its page in the browser, then compare with Expected

labels.text: Print an artifact's content, or write it to a file.

S26.07.needs: a signed-in account with at least one artifact (Managed mode)
S26.07.note: The CLI has no viewer to close or toggle, so reopening means running the same command again.
steps: Run: agi artifacts show <id> and read the output
Note that the command prints and ends, so there is nothing to close
Open a new terminal window (the reload step) and run the same command again
Compare: the same content prints with the same id

labels.text: Print an artifact's content, or write it to a file.

S26.12.needs: a signed-in account with at least two artifacts in one conversation (Managed mode)
S26.12.note: No viewer stays open in the CLI, so switching means running show again with another id.
steps: Run: agi artifacts list in an account with several artifacts
Run: agi artifacts show <first id> and read the content
Run: agi artifacts show <second id> and read the content
Compare: each command prints its own artifact's content
S26.12.where: agi artifacts list, then agi artifacts show <id>

labels.text: Browse, read and publish the artifacts in your AGI account.
Print an artifact's content, or write it to a file.

S26.16.needs: a signed-in account with at least one artifact (Managed mode)
S26.16.note: The code has no read-only state or label; read-only is only true because no artifact subcommand edits content.
steps: Run: agi artifacts --help and read the subcommand list: list, show, open, publish, published, audience, unpublish
Run: agi artifacts show <id> and confirm it only prints the content
Compare with Expected: no edit command or read-only label exists in the code for artifacts
S26.16.where: agi artifacts show <id> prints content; no artifact subcommand changes content

labels.text: Copy the content to the clipboard.

S26.30.needs: a Mac terminal with clipboard access, a signed-in account with an artifact (Managed mode)
S26.30.note: If the clipboard write fails the command reports Could not copy to the clipboard instead.
steps: Run: agi artifacts list and copy an id
Run: agi artifacts show <id> --copy
Look for the line Copied '<title>' to the clipboard.
Paste into a text editor and compare with the output of agi artifacts show <id>

labels.text: Publish an artifact to a shareable URL.
Change who can open a published artifact: public or workspace.
Take a published artifact's URL away again.

S26.31.needs: a signed-in account with an artifact (Managed mode); a workspace that can share artifacts for the workspace step
S26.31.note: No copy-link control exists; the share URL is only printed, so it must be copied by hand.
steps: Run: agi artifacts publish <id> and read the line Published '<title>' at <share URL> (opens for anyone with the link).
Run: agi artifacts audience <id> workspace and read the reply: can now be opened by workspace
Run: agi artifacts unpublish <id>, answer the prompt, and read: Unpublished artifact <id>. Its share link no longer resolves.
Run: agi artifacts published to check the state, then compare with Expected
S26.31.where: agi artifacts publish <id>, then agi artifacts audience <id> workspace, then agi artifacts unpublish <id>

labels.text: List what this account has published, with each page's audience and link.

S26.32.needs: a signed-in account with one published and one unpublished artifact (Managed mode)
S26.32.note: The code shows no explicit private label; an unpublished artifact is marked only by the absence of a published state, and agi artifacts published prints the raw visibility value.
steps: Run: agi artifacts list
Look at each row: a published artifact ends with published: anyone with the link or published: workspace
Check that an unpublished row shows no published state
Run: agi artifacts published and compare the audience of each page with Expected

labels.text: Always open the conversation it came from, even when it is published.
Open an artifact in the browser: its published page, or the conversation

S26.38.needs: a signed-in account with an artifact, and a browser on the Mac (Managed mode)
S26.38.note: Without --chat a published artifact opens its share page instead; if the browser cannot open, the terminal prints Open it yourself: <url>, and no gallery or library screen was found in the CLI.
steps: Run: agi artifacts list and copy the id of an artifact (each row also shows its conversation id)
Run: agi artifacts open <id> --chat
Look for Opened https://... in the terminal and check the browser shows that conversation
Compare with Expected
